_readme: Archaic KJV grammar: pronouns and verb forms modern English has dropped. Grouped
into form-classes, each with ONE shared note, because these are function words that
recur on most verses (saith alone is over 1200 times). At build time a class fires
once per verse in which any of its forms appears, so a verse shows a single grammar
row, not one per word. The reader keeps these in a collapsed group and does not mark
them inline, so the running text is not drowned. These are the app's own factual
notes, not sourced from a copyrighted work.
Forms are matched exact, lower-cased, whole-word, like the rest of the glossary.

classes.label: thou, thee, ye
classes.d: Archaic second person. Thou and thee are the singular you, subject and object; thy and thine are your and yours; ye is the plural you (subject). Modern English has dropped the singular/plural split and uses you and your throughout.

classes.label: hast, art, shalt
classes.d: Old second-person singular verb forms that pair with thou, marked by a -st or -est ending: hast = have, art = are, wast and wert = was and were, shalt = shall, wilt = will, dost and doest = do, hadst = had, canst = can, mayest = may.

classes.label: hath, doth, saith
classes.d: Old third-person singular forms ending in -th where modern English uses -s: hath = has, doth and doeth = does, saith = says. The same -eth ending is on many other KJV verbs (walketh, believeth), each meaning the plain modern -s form.
